cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, a family descended from Levi (1 Chronicles 6:1, 22). The singer is talking straight to God, and he doesn't even warm up. He opens with pure wonder: 'How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!'

cards.question: When it comes to the courts of the LORD, the singer says he's fine waiting. No rush at all.

cards.text: His soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD. Meanwhile, right next to God's altars, some tiny neighbors already moved in and set up house without asking ANYBODY.

cards.question: Who's found a home near God's altars, with a nest for her young?
The singer calls the people who dwell in God's house blessed, and he says they're ever praising Him.

cards.text: Then the song turns to the people whose hearts are set on pilgrimage, the trip to God's house. Friend, I didn't travel ANYWHERE for years, unless you count sliding from the front of a junk drawer to the back.

cards.question: The singer calls these travelers blessed. Where's their strength?

cards.text: On the road, these travelers pass through the Valley of Baca. And watch what happens to that valley when they come through.

cards.question: As the travelers pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of ___.
Even the autumn rain covers that valley with pools. But after that, the travelers wear out and turn back before they reach God in Zion.

cards.text: They go from strength to strength, all the way to God in Zion. Then, right in the middle of the song, the singer stops to pray: 'O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob.'

cards.question: In his prayer, the singer asks God to take notice of our shield and to look with favor on someone's face. Whose?

cards.text: Then he gets to the reason behind all this longing. Friend, this man has RUN THE NUMBERS.

cards.question: The singer says one day in God's courts is better than a thousand anywhere else.
Then he compares two places to be. He'd rather be a ___ in the house of his God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.

cards.text: Doorkeeper at God's house beats a tent with the wicked, and friend, I would've taken a job as the KNOB on my old drawer. Then the singer says the LORD God is a sun and a shield.

cards.question: The singer says the LORD gives ___ and ___.
The singer says the LORD withholds no good thing. From who?

answers.text: Those who bring the most gifts
Those who were born in Zion

cards.question: The song closes with one more blessing to the LORD of Hosts. Who does the singer say is blessed?

answers.text: The man who trusts in the LORD
The man who serves as priest
The man who builds the altar

findings.problem: The setup line calls the birds near the altars 'tiny neighbors.' That rules out the wrong answers on card 4 (the raven and the dove, the eagle and the owl), so the baker can pick the sparrow and the swallow from the hint alone.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card spends words defining 'pilgrimage' ('the trip to God's house'). That also says where the pilgrimage goes, which verse 5 doesn't state.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The question says 'these travelers,' which points back to the story card the baker can no longer see. It never says who the travelers are, such as the people whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'that valley,' which points back to the Valley of Baca on earlier cards the baker can't see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The card tells verse 7 ('They go from strength to strength, all the way to God in Zion') and verse 8, but it cites only Psalm 84:8. It should cite Psalm 84:7-8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Nothing on the cards before this one sets up the idea of choosing the humblest place in God's house. Card 13 sets up only the 'one day versus a thousand' comparison. Without that setup, picking doorkeeper over priest or ruler is guessing the wording of the line, not reasoning it out.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke compares the wrong things. In verse 10, the doorkeeper takes a lowly job at the good place, God's house. Papa Dorin says he'd take a lowly job at the junk drawer, which was his dark place, so it matches the tents of the wicked instead. The action doesn't line up, and a baker would say 'huh?' The card also opens by repeating verse 10, which card 15 just covered.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to fill in the exact words of the line 'the LORD gives grace and glory.' Nothing earlier lets them reason it out. This is the 'guess the next words' pattern the docs forbid, like the bad Psalm 23 example.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question calls verse 12 'one more blessing to the LORD of Hosts.' In the text, the singer speaks to the LORD of Hosts and calls the man who trusts in Him blessed. He doesn't give a blessing to the LORD.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
